content.title: About
content.content: Baked, canned beans are a ready‑to‑eat product made from selected bean varieties that have been thermally processed and sealed in airtight cans. The product is fully vegetarian, contains no meat or animal fats, and offers a mild aroma with a tender texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beans are one of the oldest cultivated crops, grown for more than 7,000 years.
Canning preserves most of the beans’ nutrients and flavor for a long shelf life.
Baking the beans inside the can improves their digestibility and makes them softer without additional cooking.
Vegetarian beans are often used as a protein and fiber source in meat‑free dishes.
Beans are rich in antioxidants such as flavonoids, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Beans provide about 20 g of protein per 100 g, making them an excellent protein source for vegetarians.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for blood formation and muscle function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Beans contain virtually no saturated fat, which is beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Contain B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B6, and folate aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals; soaking or fermenting before canning can mitigate this.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Canned beans often contain added salt; low‑sodium versions are recommended for those monitoring sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beans can be eaten straight from the can, added to salads, soups, stews, pasta, or used in vegetarian patties. They also heat quickly in the microwave or on the stovetop with a splash of water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, keep beans in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 3‑5 days. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration appears.
